newsitem.title: USA: Florida train report raises valid issues -- official.
newsitem.headline: Florida train report raises valid issues -- official.

text.p: A strongly critical report on Florida's proposed high-speed rail system raises valid issues that the state is still grappling with, the official in charge of the project said Wednesday.

"They've done a fairly good job of documenting some of the questions that we are engaged in reviewing," Charlie Smith, who oversees the rail project for the Florida Department of Transportation, said.

The report by the James Madison Institute said the $5.3 billion rail system was likely to cost more, carry fewer passengers and expose the state to greater financial risk than presently anticipated. It questioned the cost and usage projections and said there was a chance of default on the bonds that would be used to finance the train system.
Smith said his department supplied much of the data the institute used for the study.

"They've drawn their own conclusions based on the same data that we haven't drawn conclusions on yet," Smith said. "We think, based on the model we have, if we can get federal support for capital costs, then the system will generate over time sufficient revenues" to cover operating costs, debt service and building costs, Smith said.
The state expects to complete its review in December or January "as to how and whether to proceed with the project."
The 325-mile rail system would link Miami, Tampa and Orlando with electric trains travelling at up to 200 mph.
